summary:
I verified the Nurrow art review against the current build. Nurrow is NOT ON PAR: 6.5/10, with three majors confirmed open and no blocker.

The build checks: nurrow.glb (md5 de8d39f3, last commit 0840296a) is what the :5190 dev server serves. My own hash of every clip's sampler data matches the 534b07ff GLB of Oct 27, so no animation has changed since then. The splashes are the Oct 29 00:12 files.

Confirmed majors:
- **M1, splash:** my own 3x3 high-pass measure gives grain of 7.1-9.2 on the figure against 0.2-0.8 on the plate, and the source keeps one pose and yaw for every skin (nurrow.py:79, :105).
- **M2, recall:** a 2 s loop played through the 7 s recall. The arms are held still (upper arms 0.0 degrees) and the chest moves 1.0 degree. The brief asks for exactly this minimal pose (nurrow.md:121), so the gap is in the brief. Peers fill the same channel with a performance: Burdam 6 s, Ervet 9 s.
- **M3, cloak:** 97 % of the cloak's vertex weight is on x_cape_1/2, and fighters have no runtime cloth. The cloak swings 1.2 / 0.7 degrees in the run, because the authored drive is only plus or minus 3 degrees and the spring is critically damped (zeta 0.97).

Downgraded: M4 (materials) goes to minor. Its numbers reproduce: the hat's roughness is 0.70-0.72, and the normal map is the flattest in the roster, with 2.8 % of texels over 10 degrees against 11.6-18.2 % for seven peers. The read claim does not hold at the gameplay camera, though. Every material separates and reads as what it is:
- the hat shows gores and a lit and a shaded side (core L* sd 2.0-2.8);
- the wood shows grain;
- the cloth shows painted folds.
None of them reads as the wrong material. Dunsom's flat hat disc, a confirmed major, measures 1.3-1.5. What is left is a polish gap: the lacquer has no sheen.

Corrections to the review: the channel clip has 38 keys over 1.33 s, not 2 keys, and Nurrow's kit has no channel ability, so that part carries little weight. Sensitivity is clean, re-checked on all three skins: the hat is a wide brim cone (PCA 0.30 m tall by 0.82 m wide), the hood lies down at the back of the neck and is round, and every mask is a carved, living smiling face. All four _open.json leftovers are still open.

findings.title: Splashes and portraits are grainy static model renders on painted plates, in one victory stand for all three skins
findings.what: Base, Noon Fair and Shadeprint splashes are one render: the victory hold at t 0.92, yaw 22, set in the right third of the frame on a painted plate. The figure carries render grain that the plate does not have, and its light does not match the plate. The base and Noon Fair portraits share one pose and one framing.
findings.evidence:
- Viewed: art/out/fighters/nurrow/splash.png, nurrow_noon_fair_splash.png and nurrow_shadeprint_splash.png (Oct 29 00:12), side by side.
- My 3x3 high-pass luma std (closing_nurrow_ver_measure.txt): the figure's cloak measures 7.4 / 7.6 / 7.1 and the trousers 8.4 / 7.8 / 9.2. The plate measures 0.21-0.35 in the sky and 0.79-0.84 in the midground.
- Source: nurrow.py:79 SPLASH = victory / 0.92 / yaw 22. nurrow.py:105 reads 'The splash keeps the bible's pose, yaw and hero pitch'.
- Crops: _harness/_shots/closing_nurrow_splash_head_x2.png and closing_nurrow_portraits_3up.png.
findings.gauge: A recent League champion gets a painted splash for every skin, each with its own pose, composition and scene. Its lighting is unified with the background, and the portraits are crops of those paintings.
findings.fix:
Give each skin its own key moment from Nurrow's world:
- **Base:** the hush over a guttering street lamp.
- **Noon Fair:** under the fair's paper lanterns, with lacquer moths lifting off the brim.
- **Shadeprint:** a woodblock composition with violet sleep-shadows pooling from her feet.

Render at high samples with a denoiser, and match the key and rim light to each plate. Then do a 2D paint-over pass and crop the portraits from it.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed with my own measurement. Figure grain is about 10-35x the plate's. The pose is fixed in source for every skin, by design ('keeps the bible's pose'), so the cause is the pipeline's spec. This is the same roster-wide major that the Ardit, Ervet, Kemdo, Lisvel and Hesmi verifiers confirmed, and against the gauge it holds here too.

findings.title: Recall is a frozen 2 s loop played through the 7 s recall (channel likewise near-static)
findings.what: The recall is one held pose: blade lowered, hand at the chest. Small oscillations on the chest, neck and head are added, and the 2 s clip loops about 3.5 times through RIFT's 7 s recall. The arms never move. The channel is a 1.33 s loop that moves no bone more than 3.2 degrees.
findings.evidence:
- My GLB decode (closing_nurrow_ver_measure.txt), as max from frame 0 / max pairwise:
  - recall (2.0 s): upper_arm.L/R 0.0 / 0.0, chest 1.0 / 2.0, head 3.6 / 7.2, hand.R 3.5 / 6.9 degrees, hips 0, cape 0.7 degrees;
  - channel (1.333 s, 38 keys): every bone at or under 2.0 / 3.2 degrees.
- Source: nurrow.py:3004-3015 (rec pose plus anim.osc at 1-3 degrees).
- Looping: src/render/actors.ts:128 lists recall in LOOPING; content/modes.json:28 sets recallTime 7.
- Roster (_harness/_reports/closing_dunsom_idle_roster_cmp.txt): Burdam's recall is 6.0 s with chest 14.8 degrees and hand 81 cm, and Ervet's is 9.0 s, so the pipeline can author a full recall.
findings.gauge: A recent League champion's recall is its own multi-second performance that fills the whole channel. VALE shows a 2 s held pose on loop.
findings.files: art/blender/fighters/nurrow.py:3004-3015; _design/fighters/nurrow.md:121; src/render/actors.ts:118,128 (only if a one-shot recall role is needed)
findings.verifierNote:
Confirmed as a major, resting on the recall. Two corrections:
- The channel is 38 keys over 1.333 s, not '2 keys'. Nurrow's kit has no channel ability (content/fighters/nurrow.json only maps the clip), so the channel adds little weight.
- The recall follows its brief exactly ('lowers the blade and hums with a hand over her heart', nurrow.md:121). The fix has to go through the brief.

This is consistent with the Dunsom and Ilsheta verdicts.

findings.title: The knee-length felt cloak is a rigid board in run, dash and idle
findings.what: The model ships a felt cloak that runs from the shoulders to below the knees. The brief describes 0.30 m rigid mantle points instead. The cloak is driven only by the x_cape chain. In the run, the most-seen clip, it hangs as one sheet that is lifted back and turns with the chest.
findings.gauge: A League champion's long cloth lags and kicks through the run cycle and settles in idle, visibly, at the gameplay camera. VALE's cloak moves 1-2 cm.
findings.fix:
Make the per-step drive in the run pose plus or minus 10-12 degrees (not 3), phased off the foot contacts. Lower the damping to about 9 so the hem overshoots. Split the hem into left and right chains so the ragged points flick out of phase.

Targets: 10-15 degrees in run, 3-5 in idle, 20 or more in dash. Keep the floor collision and the lunge gravity. Update brief §1/§4 to describe the cloak as shipped.
findings.verifierNote:
Confirmed and sharpened. The reviewer blamed only the spring tuning, but the authored run drive is itself only plus or minus 3 degrees, and inertia cannot help an in-place clip. Both need changing.

The brief does ask for rigid points, but the cloak that shipped is knee-length felt, and a cloak of that size reading as a board is a gauge gap. This is consistent with Ardit-M3, Burdam-M5 and Kemdo-M4.

findings.title: Lacquer hat and carved mask have no gloss; the normal map is the roster's flattest (materials otherwise separate)
findings.evidence:
- Reproduced: hat ORM-G p10/50/90 0.70 / 0.71 / 0.72, and normal-map tilt p50 0.3 degrees with 2.8 % of texels over 10 degrees. The other seven fighters measured have 11.6-18.2 % over 10 degrees (_harness/_reports/closing_nurrow_ver_albedo_cmp.txt).
- In match (closing_nurrow_ver_measure.txt): hat core L* sd 2.0 / 2.0 / 2.8. The 30-degree sector means span 80.2-85.3, a lit and a shaded side, with gore strokes visible. Dunsom's hat, a confirmed major, measures sd 1.3-1.5 and is flat to 0.7 R.
- Side by side: _harness/_shots/closing_nurrow_ver_hat_vs_dunsom.png.
- Albedo extracted from the GLB: wood rings on the pauldron and mask, painted cloth folds, radial gores on the hat.
- Portraits (closing_nurrow_portrait_faces_x2.png): the mask's carved facets and grain read.
findings.gauge: League's material identity lives in the hand-painted diffuse: lacquer gets a painted highlight band and darker seams. VALE's materials separate in hue, value and painted pattern, but the lacquer never reads as glossy.
findings.fix: Paint a sheen band on the lacquer's lit side and darker gore seams, and lower its roughness to about 0.35-0.40, keeping the lit end at or below L* 85 (see _open#2). Add gloss to the mask's brow shelf and cheek planes. Re-bake the normal map with the gore stitching, rim rivets and felt nap. It is the flattest in the roster at the same 512 budget, so this costs nothing in size.
findings.files: art/blender/fighters/nurrow.py:81 (TEXTURE_SIZES), :1203-1230 and the _lacquer brushwork; the ORM/normal bake
findings.verifierNote:
Downgraded to minor. The numbers reproduce, and I add one the reviewer missed: the normal map is about 5x flatter than any peer's. The claim 'everything reads as one matte finish' does not hold at the gameplay camera, which is where the gauge is read.

No material reads as the wrong material. The hat is clearly structured, unlike Dunsom's flat disc. The Lisvel verifier independently cited Nurrow as an example of painted plates and fold shading under the same budget.

What remains is the lacquer's missing gloss, polish-level like Ardit-M4. Most of the 'grainy felt' in the store art is M1's render grain.

findings.title: The hat has no value headroom, and the felt drifts toward rose (mostly in the store art)
findings.what: The lit end of the lacquer sits in the tone map's shoulder. The felt drifts warm: a little in match, a lot in the splash.
findings.evidence:
- Hat: L* p98 86.6-87.8, p50 83.6-83.9 in match.
- Felt in match: the brief's cloth #796265 is L* 44, C* 10, hab 10. The match body measures hab 19, C* 12.7-15.4 (closing_nurrow_ingame_measure.txt).

findings.gauge: A League champion's palette holds from the store art to the match.
findings.fix: Lower the lacquer's lit end 2-3 L*. Correct the store-light tint on the felt so the splash cloak stays near hab 10.
findings.verifierNote: Kept, with a correction: the in-match drift is small (9 degrees of hue). The clear drift is in the splash and portraits.

findings.evidence:
_harness/_reports/closing_nurrow_fk_tip.txt, death clip:

findings.title: The face reads sly rather than asleep; the chip backdrop is in Tunlan's magenta family
findings.what: The carved lids read as half-open eyes glancing sideways, not closed. The chip's backdrop hue sits close to Tunlan's.
findings.evidence:
- Lids: _harness/_shots/closing_nurrow_portrait_faces_x2.png and closing_nurrow_icon_sizes_x3.png (viewed).
- Chip (closing_nurrow_chip_cmp.txt): the border hab is 332 for Nurrow and 324 for Tunlan, but L* is 18 vs 28 and C* 18 vs 36. The per-pixel dE76 at 32 px is 37.9, in line with the other pairs (35-47).
findings.gauge: A League champion's portrait shows the intended expression at a glance.
findings.fix: Deepen the downward curve of the lid carving and add an ink lash line so the lids read as closed. Shift the chip's backdrop hue at least 20 degrees from Tunlan's.
findings.files: art/blender/fighters/nurrow.py (mask lids); the icon/chip backdrop table
findings.verifierNote: Kept. The chip half is weak: the two chips separate as well as other pairs do. The lid read is the real part.

findings.title: The atlas is fragmented, the maps are low-res, and some metalness remains
findings.what: The smart-UV atlas breaks into confetti islands. The ORM is 256 and the normal map 512. Some texels carry metalness, which the brief forbids (metalness 0 everywhere).
findings.evidence:
- Albedo extracted from the GLB: confetti island bands along the top and right of the atlas.
- Metalness: 1.86 % of ORM texels have metal over 0.1, with a maximum of 0.227 (closing_nurrow_material_maps.txt, reproduced).
- Thin orange seam lines cross the Shadeprint cowl and trousers in the close-up: _harness/_shots/closing_nurrow_ver_backcowl_shade.png.
findings.gauge: League champions use clean, efficient atlases with no visible seams.
findings.fix: Zero the metal channel at bake. Repack the atlas with larger islands for the hat, cloak and mask. Dilate the islands in the skin recolour so the seams do not show.
findings.verifierNote: Kept. Map sizes are a roster budget (normal 512 on every fighter), and the seam lines are only visible in the close-up.
